thread:
achira: Brought zelos-v1 to canary and did a quick multilingual onboarding run. Notable regression on the JP+AR mixed-orientation subset when running int8 quant: BLEU down ~2.8 vs fp16 and we have odd spacing inside ruby brackets and reversed parentheses order for Arabic.

nora: Can you paste a tiny repro + the eval metrics?

achira: repro input used in the smoke set:
```
日本語（漢字《ふりがな》）とArabic (مرحبا)
```
int8 model output (truncated):
```
日本語（漢字《ふ り が な 》）とArabic )مرحبا(
```

Note: spaces inserted between the kana inside the U+300A/U+300B brackets and the Arabic parentheses appear after the Arabic text instead of wrapping the Arabic (i.e., mirrored).

mike: fp16 baseline?

achira: fp16 clean. This shows only on our int8 build path in canary. I re-ran with q5_0 and q4_0 for comparison: q5_0 = slightly off but much better than int8; q4_0 = similar to fp16. So it looks quant-mode sensitive and worst in int8.

eval-bot: [automated] job=7859012345-A subset=mix-orient BLEU(fp16)=30.1 BLEU(int8)=27.3 chrF(fp16)=0.615 chrF(int8)=0.582 sample_mismatch=74/1000

ling: Could this be a tokenizer vocab or merge table change? If tokenization changed we'd see different token ids pre-decode. Please run `python -m token_inspect --text "\u3075\u308a\u304c" --tokenizer zelos-v1-tokenizer` and attach ids.

achira: did that. Token ids for the furigana span:
```
# fp16 tokens: [4231, 78, 332]
# int8 tokens: [4231, 300, 78, 332]
```
So int8 path emits an extra merge boundary token id=300 (which corresponds to a SPACE token in our vocab).

nora: Interesting. That suggests something upstream of detok: tokens differ. Why would quant change emitted token ids? Quant shouldn't affect tokenization. Possibilities: (1) model logits near merge boundary flip due to quant error, (2) greedy/beam decoding tie-breaks altered by different softmax scaling, (3) decode-time byte alignment bug that inserts a codepoint interpreted as space.

mike: Can you dump the raw byte stream from the int8 decoder (hex) around the ruby brackets? If there's an accidental 0x20 or a ZWSP U+200B we can see it.

achira: Hex snippet captured from int8 decode buffer (UTF-8 bytes): ... e3 81 85 20 e3 81 8a ... which maps to an ASCII 0x20 between multibyte chars. fp16 run doesn't show the 0x20.

runtime-bot: Noted: runtime image tag for canary is runtime@sha256:abcdef1234 (built 2024-12-02). Recent change: `decode_buffer_align` optimization merged in runtime-2024-11-29.

ling: That aligns with my memory — decode_buffer_align touches memcpy/unaligned loads on our decode kernels and could produce stray zero bytes on certain kernel code paths. If those bytes are interpreted as tokens they will produce space tokens.

nora: Plan: (A) bisect runtime commits around `decode_buffer_align` to confirm, (B) add a smoke unit that asserts no ASCII space bytes are inserted between UTF-8 multi-byte sequences during decode for mixed-direction strings, (C) run int8 with `--disable-decode-alignment` flag if runtime supports it.

achira: I've run a quick kernel-level repro enabling `--disable-decode-alignment` and int8 output matches fp16 (no extra spaces, parentheses orientation correct). So this pins it to the runtime decode alignment change.

mike: Great repro. Can you capture the failing kernel logs and the minimal C snippet that triggers misaligned copy? We should open a runtime bug with reproducer + CI test.

runtime-bot: Suggested interim mitigation: pin runtime to pre-2024-11-29 image or set `decode_alignment=1` at startup to force safe path.

nora: I'll open the bisect PR and a tiny unit test in runtime repo. If fix requires careful memcpy semantics we'll patch or guard the optimized path behind a quant-safe check. Also add a brief note in the canary release notes about potential mixed-orientation detok issues for int8 until backported.

achira: Thank you. I'll upload the small repro tarball (100 samples + token_inspect outputs + decode hex) to the triage ticket and update the canary rollback doc if needed. :thumbsup:

mike: Once runtime patch lands we should run a full multilingual smoke with extra locale combos (JP+HE, KR+AR, ZH+AR) to ensure no other bidi boundaries are affected.

ling: Also add a short eval to compare greedy vs beam tie-breaker behavior under quant to rule out decoding rule interactions.

nora: Sounds like a plan. Tagging infra to hold the runtime pin until runtime fix is validated. Keep updates here.

achira: will follow up with repro link in the ticket.
